subject: Audit evidence: operator-change ledger, export idempotency & proofing
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@medicosys.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request — operator-change ledger export and integrity checks

Jonas / Redwood team,

We're preparing for a SIG/SOC2 readiness window and need to validate the operator-change / admin-action ledger for a recent production tranche. Specifically: what fields are captured for operator/admin actions (user id, action type, target resource, timestamp, request_id/kvcache pointer, prior_state hash), how long those events are retained, and what export options you support for an attested handoff.

Can you provide a short deliverable that includes: a sample export slice (CSV or JSONL) covering ~7 days, a manifest with checksums and sequence numbers so we can verify idempotent replays, and a description of available transports (SFTP with signed manifest, presigned S3 with HMAC, or DocuSign attestation). Also include the SLA for producing the initial package and the ability to re-run the same export window with deterministic checksums.

Attachments: none on this side yet.

Thanks — tight timeline on our end, can you confirm by EOD today?

Sarah Li
Senior Compliance Manager
MedicoSys

From: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@medicosys.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 12:40:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — operator-change ledger export and integrity checks

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. We can produce that. High-level response and proposed next steps below.

What we will include:
- Sample export: operator_changes_sample.csv (CSV with columns: event_id, timestamp_utc, operator_user_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, prior_state_hash, request_id, sequence_index)
- Manifest: manifest-checksums.txt (SHA256 per file + overall signed envelope)
- Export handshake: export-handshake.md (options: SFTP with PGP-signed manifest, presigned S3 + HMAC verification, or DocuSign attestation of manifest)

Determinism and replays:
- Exports are windowed and idempotent for the same timebox as long as no retention compaction occurs. Each export includes a sequence_index and server-generated export_nonce so you can verify replays. We will also include event-level monotonic sequence numbers.

Retention and scope:
- Operator/admin action events kept for 365 days by default; 7-year retention available as an enterprise option (requires provisioning). Some ephemeral entries (e.g., volatile debug traces) are excluded from the canonical ledger and are not part of the export.

Timeline / SLA:
- Initial sample package: 48 hours from confirmation.
- Full on-demand export (larger window) turnaround: 5 business days (subject to capacity scheduling).

Requested confirmation from you:
1) Target window (start/end UTC) for the sample slice (we'll default to most recent 7 days).
2) Preferred transport (SFTP pgp, presigned S3, or DocuSign attestation).

Attached: operator_changes_sample.csv (stub), manifest-checksums.txt (stub), export-handshake.md (handshake options and public key fingerprints).

On internal next steps, I've looped in Kimberly and Vanessa to finalize the signed envelope and to coordinate the export job.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Manager, Compliance & Security
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 13:05:37 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evidence request — operator-change ledger export and integrity checks

Kimberly / Vanessa — forwarding Sarah's ask. Key implementation notes for the export job: 

- Export format: CSV preferred by the customer; include header with column types and UTC timestamps.
- Deterministic ordering: sort by sequence_index then event_id. Include export_nonce in manifest and sign manifest with our KMS key (key-id: projects/redwood/keys/export-v1).
- Checksum approach: SHA256 per file + manifest-level SHA256 of concatenated file shas, include timestamp and signer id.
- Idempotency: We'll create an export record in the control plane with a stable export_id for the requested timebox. Re-running the same export_id must produce identical files unless retention/compression intervenes. Need to confirm that retention compaction can't delete events in the requested window (we should mark export window as 'preserved' for 72 hours post-delivery).
- Redaction: For SIG/SOC2, we should not redact operator_usernames, but we must mask ephemeral debug tokens. The canonical ledger contains user_id hashes for internal consistency and a mapping file for auditor review on request (requires NDA).

Action items:
1) Kimberly: please confirm the KMS signing key and whether we can auto-generate a PGP signed manifest (I think we can).
2) Vanessa: schedule export worker slot for Thursday AM to meet the 48h SLA if Sarah confirms today.

I'll attach the handshake doc here for quick review.

Jonas

Thanks, Jonas — that plan works. Please proceed with the sample for the most recent 7-day window (2026-06-17T00:00:00Z to 2026-06-24T00:00:00Z) and use presigned S3 + manifest signed with your KMS key. We'll validate the manifest and checksums on receipt.

Two quick clarifications:
- Can you add the request_id field for each event (useful for correlating with our incident tickets)?
- We need the export_nonce and export_id included in the manifest metadata so our tooling can deterministically match previous runs.

If you can provide the sample within your 48h SLA, we'll schedule an intake review in our audit tracker and follow up with any deeper requests. Also please send the DocuSign attestation option if presigned S3 is not acceptable for the final handoff.

Thanks,
Sarah Li
